newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen up on USDA data- trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen up on USDA data- trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen higher following Friday's USDA quarterly hog inventory report, which showed smaller-than-expected hog supplies, livestock dealers said.

Bullish reaction to the report in the Chicago Mercantile Exchange live hog and pork belly futures will support cash hog prices early next week, but it was unknown by how much, said Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp. of Iowa.
"I don't know what cash is going to trade Monday, if they think its going to be limit-up for two days," Maher said, "They'll have a hell of a time getting hogs," he said.
Maher added that producers will likely hang onto hogs rather than sell them right away, knowing that prices were on the rise.

USDA showed all hogs on U.S. farms as of December 1 at 96 percent of a year ago, hogs kept for breeding at 97 percent and hogs kept for market at 96 percet, all of which were less than what most analysts expected.

Hogs had been called mostly steady for Monday before the report. Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota had been expected to range $54.50 to $55.00. Illinois top plant prices had been seen at $54.50.
Indiana and Ohio top prices for hogs shipped to the plant had been expected steady at $53.00 to $54.00, livestock dealers said.
